data.narrative:
Thunder Tiger, a Defense & Security company at the public stage, has raised $22M+ as of 2025. The valuation universe comprises 26 same-sector peers, including 2 public comparables (DRSHF, IDEAFORGE.NS) and 8 private peers spanning Evolv Technology, Anduril Industries, Helsing, Castelion, and Shield AI.

Peer-median methodology is not applicable here. The narrow peer set—filtered by stage alignment, adjacent-stage proximity, and valuation-tier similarity—yields fewer than three datapoints necessary for robust triangulation. While 26 Defense & Security peers exist in aggregate, none satisfy the stringent same-stage or adjacent-stage criteria with comparable valuation profiles. Applying an all-sector median would introduce material bias given Thunder Tiger's specialized position within Defense & Security.

The absence of a sufficient narrow peer cohort constrains quantitative valuation support from conventional comparable-company analysis. Any defensible valuation range would require either (1) relaxing stage or tier filters at the cost of methodological precision, or (2) deploying alternative approaches—such as precedent transaction analysis within Defense & Security, discounted cash flow modeling if operational data exists, or venture capital method calibration against funding rounds. Key uncertainties include Thunder Tiger's revenue scale, margin profile relative to public Defense & Security names, and path to sustained profitability. Without these operational metrics or a sufficiently tight peer universe, a specific valuation range cannot be anchored to the data provided.
